inline_comments.comment:
The grammar rule `| INVALID { $$=[]; }` makes invalid participant syntax a valid parse result — jison will NOT throw, the parse simply succeeds with an empty line. Because `Diagram.fromText` performs no post-parse validation (it just calls `await parser.parse(text)` and immediately returns `new Diagram(...)`), the function will return normally when this input is encountered. This directly contradicts the test at line 2622, which asserts `expect(error).toBe(true)` — no error is thrown, so `error` stays `false` and the test will fail.

The two changes are inconsistent: either (a) remove `| INVALID { $$=[]; }` from the grammar and let jison emit a parse error (which propagates as a throw from `Diagram.fromText`), or (b) keep the silent-discard behaviour but fix the test to assert that no error is thrown and that the invalid participant is simply absent from the diagram.

When an `INVALID` token is silently swallowed here, no warning or error is emitted. The PR description promises "a clear console error instead of causing recursion", but neither a `log.warn(...)` call nor a `throw` is present anywhere in the grammar action or in `sequenceDb`. Per the project's conventions, soft-constraint violations that produce degraded output should call `log.warn` so that users and developers have actionable feedback about why a participant was silently dropped. Consider adding a call such as `yy.parseError('Invalid participant syntax — angle brackets are not allowed in participant names', {});` or a `log.warn(...)` in a grammar action here.

The new character class `[^<>:\n,;@]` is narrower than what the original patterns excluded. The original first rule used `[^\<->\->:\n,;@]`, where `\<->` is a character-range from `<` (ASCII 60) to `>` (ASCII 62), covering `<`, `=`, and `>`, plus a separate literal `\-` exclusion — effectively excluding `<`, `=`, `>`, and `-`. The new rules allow `-` (and `=`) in participant names. This is likely a positive usability improvement, but it is a behavioural change that is not mentioned in the PR description or changeset. Existing diagrams where an author accidentally included a `-` in a participant declaration may now parse differently. Please document this in the changeset or PR description.
The file is missing a trailing newline (`\ No newline at end of file` in the diff). All text files in this project should end with a newline to satisfy POSIX conventions and avoid noisy diffs.

The test description "should handle fail parsing when alias token causes conflicts in participant definition" is misleading. The actual problem is that angle brackets (`<`, `>`) appear in a participant name (e.g., `
` used as inline HTML), not an alias-token conflict. A clearer description would be something like: `'should throw when a participant name contains angle brackets (e.g. HTML tags)'`.

The try/catch + boolean flag pattern is less idiomatic than the Vitest/Jest `rejects` API and produces less informative failure messages. Prefer: ```js await expect( Diagram.fromText(` sequenceDiagram participant SAS MyServiceWithMoreThan20Chars
service decription `) ).rejects.toThrow(); ``` This is the standard pattern used in this project for async error assertions and makes the intent immediately clear.

general_comments.comment: The core fix (replacing the catastrophically-backtracking regexes `[^\<->\->:\n,;@]+?([\ -]*[^\<->\->:\n,;@]+?)*?` with simple, anchored patterns) is exactly the right approach and correctly targets the ReDoS root cause. However, the PR conflates two incompatible goals: (1) silently ignore invalid lines and continue rendering, and (2) throw an error to alert the user. The grammar change implements (1); the test asserts (2); the PR description describes (2). These need to be reconciled — pick one strategy and make both the grammar and the test reflect it consistently.

The new test only checks that *some* error was thrown (`expect(error).toBe(true)`), not which error or what message it carries. Even if the implementation is corrected to actually throw, the test should assert on the specific error type or message (e.g., `.rejects.toThrow(/invalid participant/i)`) so that future regressions — such as a different, unrelated parse error masking the intended one — are not silently accepted as a passing test.
